answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Ledger. Each identity must leave a verifiable record of prior actions that a new identity cannot inherit, checked against the previous epoch's ledger before it can transact. An identity that has no ledge of past behaviour starts at zero trust and cannot act until it accumulates history. Sybils must therefore operate identities across multiple epochs to build usable history, and any identity that seems to wander between unrelated task clusters is flagged. A sharp karst of inconsistent behaviour between epochs triggers exclusion.
